sections.h2: How is South Carolina organized when you sell a house?
sections.html:
South Carolina has 46 counties, the most the state allows by law, and nearly every step of a home sale runs through a county office. The city you live in matters less than the county it sits in. A Charleston address, for example, can touch Charleston County or Berkeley County records, and Greenville County is the state's most populous county even though Charleston is the largest city.

Three county offices come up in almost every sale:

  • The assessor and auditor, who set the value and the tax bill.
  • The treasurer or delinquent tax collector, who takes payment and chases overdue accounts.
  • The register of deeds or clerk of court, who records the deed that moves title to the buyer.

Below you will find our pages grouped by county, with local property tax guides first and city pages after them. If your county is not listed, the rules on this page still apply and the county offices can answer local questions. For a full list of our local pages, see South Carolina guides by city and county.

sections.h2: Who collects property tax, and what happens if it is overdue at closing?
sections.html:
Property tax in South Carolina is administered and collected locally, with the Department of Revenue assisting counties. Taxes are due between September 30 and January 15, and penalties start after that: 3 percent, then an additional 7 percent from February 2, then an additional 5 percent from March 17. After that the account goes to execution.

The assessment ratio depends on how the house is used. An owner-occupied legal residence, with up to five contiguous acres, is assessed at 4 percent of fair market value. Other real property, a rental house for example, is assessed at 6 percent. Counties must reappraise and equalize once every fifth year, so a sale price can land in a reassessment year and a bill can jump.

If tax stays unpaid, the county can sell the property at a delinquent tax sale. The owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor then has 12 months to redeem. Interest runs 3 percent in months one to three, 6 percent in months four to six, 9 percent in months seven to nine and 12 percent in the last three, figured on the bid. Selling before that sale is almost always cleaner for everyone. Our South Carolina property tax guide walks through appeals and selling with tax due.

sections.h2: How does recording a deed work here, and what does it cost?
sections.html:
A deed is recorded with the register of deeds in 25 counties and with the clerk of court in the other 21. The register counties include Charleston, Greenville, Richland, Horry, Lexington and Spartanburg. Counties such as York and Union use the clerk of court instead, so check which office your county uses before you send papers.

Before a deed can be recorded, the signing must be proved by a witness affidavit or acknowledged by the grantor in front of two witnesses. The register records instruments in the order presented once execution is proved.

The deed recording fee is $1.85 for each $500 of value, split into $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county. The office usually asks for an affidavit stating the value of the property, or the reason the deed is exempt. Several transfers are exempt, including:

  • A deed in lieu of foreclosure or a deed out of a foreclosure case to the mortgagee.
  • A corrective or quitclaim deed that only confirms title already held, with no payment.
  • Some transfers to or from a trust or between close family members where nothing is paid beyond the ownership interest.
  • A distribution deed from an estate to its heirs.

Ask the county office about its own filing fees and formatting rules. We cover the basics in our recording a deed guide and the quitclaim deed page.

sections.h2: How does foreclosure work in South Carolina?
sections.html:
South Carolina foreclosures go through the courts. Under Title 29, a lender generally has to establish the debt by court judgment before a mortgagee's sale can pass title, or the borrower must consent in writing after the loan matures. The judge can enter the judgment and order the sale together.

In many counties a master in equity runs the sale. Richland County, for example, holds its sales on the first Monday of each month at the Central Courthouse in Columbia, and the winning bidder other than the plaintiff owes a 5 percent deposit by 3:00 p.m. that day. Other counties set their own schedules, so confirm with the master in equity's office.

A deficiency judgment can follow if the owner is personally liable for what the sale did not cover. A defendant facing one has 30 days after the sale to petition for an appraisal, which can reduce or cancel the deficiency. Selling before the sale date lets an owner skip that exposure, and a cash buyer who closes fast can fit inside a short window. Talk to a South Carolina attorney about your own case.

sections.h2: What should heirs know about selling an inherited house?
sections.html:
An inherited house usually goes through the probate court of the county where the person lived. The small estate affidavit is a shortcut, and it has limits. It can be used 30 days after death, but only if the whole probate estate, after liens, is $45,000 or less, and it collects personal property. It does not convey a house.

For a house, the personal representative is the person with authority to sign. Our probate guide explains how the court appointment and the deed of distribution fit together. The deed that distributes real estate to an heir is not charged the usual deed recording fee, and no value affidavit is required for it.

Heirs who cannot agree, or who live out of state, often find that a sale lets everyone settle without carrying the house. Keep the taxes current while the estate is open, since the delinquent tax clock does not stop for probate. See also our notes on estate and inheritance tax.

sections.h2: Can you sell a South Carolina house with tenants in it?
sections.html:
Yes. A sale does not end a lease on its own, so the buyer takes the house with the tenancy unless it is ended properly first. The main notice periods in the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act are:

  • Unpaid rent: the tenant has five days from the due date, then the landlord can terminate after written notice.
  • Other lease breaches: termination no sooner than 14 days after the tenant receives notice, if the breach is not fixed.
  • Week-to-week tenancy: at least 7 days of written notice.
  • Month-to-month tenancy: at least 30 days of written notice.

Security deposits need a plan. After a good faith sale, the seller stays liable for the deposit unless it is transferred to the buyer, and the tenant must be told in writing within a reasonable time. Only a court order can remove a tenant who stays after the notice period. Read our guides on the eviction process, eviction notices and landlord and tenant rights before you list a rental.

sections.h2: What does a cash as-is sale mean in South Carolina?
sections.html:
It means the buyer pays cash, does not ask the seller for repairs and does not wait on a lender's appraisal. The sale still has to be done correctly. South Carolina's Supreme Court held in Doe v. McMaster that real estate closings should be conducted only under the supervision of attorneys, so expect a South Carolina attorney to handle the title search, the closing and the recording instructions in most deals.

Most sellers of one to four unit homes must hand the buyer a property condition disclosure statement before the contract is signed. It covers the roof, foundation, plumbing, wood destroying insects, radon and similar items. The form lets the owner state that no representation is made about a condition, though knowingly false answers can bring liability for damages. Transfers by an estate's fiduciary, court ordered sales and foreclosures are exempt, and the buyer and seller may also agree in writing to skip the form.

Cash buyers, ourselves included, buy houses in many conditions. The paperwork above stays the same whether the house is tidy or needs work. We do not promise a price here, since that depends on the property.

sections.h2: Does the homestead exemption affect a sale?
sections.html: It can. The first $50,000 of fair market value of a dwelling is exempt from county, municipal, school and special assessment taxes for owners who are 65 or older, totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind. Owners apply through the county auditor, and failing to apply waives the exemption for that year. A buyer will not inherit your exemption, so expect the tax bill to change after closing. Details are on our homestead exemption page.

faqs.q: How many counties does South Carolina have?
faqs.a: South Carolina has 46 counties, the maximum the state allows. Property tax, deeds and probate are handled at the county level, so start with the county where the house sits.

faqs.q: When are South Carolina property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due between September 30 and January 15. A 3 percent penalty applies after that, with further penalties on February 2 and March 17 before the account goes to execution.

faqs.q: Is foreclosure in South Carolina handled by a court?
faqs.a: Yes. A lender generally has to establish the debt by court judgment before the sale can pass title, and many counties hold sales through a master in equity.

faqs.q: Who records a deed in South Carolina?
faqs.a: The register of deeds in 25 counties, or the clerk of court in the other 21. The recording fee is $1.85 per $500 of value unless the deed is exempt.

faqs.q: Can I use a small estate affidavit to sell an inherited house?
faqs.a: No. The affidavit covers personal property up to $45,000 and does not convey real estate. A house goes through the probate court and the personal representative.

faqs.q: Do I need an attorney to close a sale in South Carolina?
faqs.a: In practice yes. The state's Supreme Court has said closings should be conducted only under attorney supervision, so an attorney usually handles the title work and closing.

faqs.q: What notice ends a month-to-month tenancy?
faqs.a: At least 30 days of written notice. Week-to-week tenancies need at least 7 days.

faqs.q: Where do I find the county office for my house?
faqs.a: Use the county sections on this page. They link to local guides and city pages, and the county office can confirm fees and forms.
